name: aw_dev_fade_in
prose: Precondition: aw_dev is the amplifier with volume_desc, fade_step and fade_in_time set. Returns nothing. It targets fade_in_vol = volume_desc.ctl_volume. If fade_step is 0 or fade_in_time is 0 it calls aw_dev_set_volume(aw_dev, fade_in_vol) once and returns. Otherwise it calls aw_dev_set_volume(aw_dev, i) for i = AW88399_MUTE_VOL (1023) decreasing by fade_step while i >= fade_in_vol, sleeping fade_in_time to fade_in_time + 10 microseconds after each call; after the loop, if i is not exactly fade_in_vol, it calls aw_dev_set_volume once more with fade_in_vol. aw_dev_set_volume's return value is ignored; it computes min(value + init_volume, AW88399_MUTE_VOL), reads SYSCTRL2 and, only if the read succeeds, writes the new volume bits combined with the preserved other bits. So the last register write has volume min(fade_in_vol + init_volume, 1023) but is skipped if that read fails. fade_step is only tested against 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function aw88399.c:779-798, aw_dev_set_volume (757-777). Reviewer right (init_volume added, other bits preserved, no write on read error).

name: cs35l41_get_fs_mon_config_index
prose: Precondition: freq is a frequency in Hz. Scans the table cs35l41_fs_mon in order and returns the index of the first entry whose freq field equals freq, or -EINVAL if no entry matches. It reads only that constant table and has no side effects.
note: cs35l41.c:156-166. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits EINVAL), right; contract left empty because of the table lookup.

name: cs35l45_get_clk_freq_id
prose: Precondition: freq is a reference clock frequency in Hz. Returns -EINVAL immediately if freq is 0. Otherwise it scans cs35l45_pll_refclk_freq in order and returns the cfg_id field (not the table index) of the first entry whose freq equals freq, or -EINVAL if none matches. No side effects.
note: cs35l45-tables.c:318-331. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits EINVAL), right; contract left empty because of the table lookup.

name: cs35l45_amplifier_mode_put
prose: Precondition: kcontrol belongs to the cs35l45 component and ucontrol->value.integer.value[0] is the requested amplifier mode (AMP_MODE_SPK or AMP_MODE_RCV). Returns 0 without changing anything if the requested mode equals cs35l45->amplifier_mode or is greater than AMP_MODE_RCV. Otherwise it takes the DAPM mutex, reads CS35L45_BLOCK_ENABLES (on a read error it unlocks and returns that negative error, with nothing changed), clears the amplifier enable bit, disables the "SPK" pin and syncs DAPM. For AMP_MODE_SPK it clears the receiver enable bit, enables the boost, sets the HVLV mode to operation and activates the "Analog PCM Volume" control; for the other mode (RCV) it sets the receiver enable, disables the boost, forces low-voltage operation, clears the DRE enable bit, sets the PCM amp gain to 13 dBV and deactivates the "Analog PCM Volume" control. A failure of cs35l45_activate_ctl is only logged. If the amplifier enable bit had been set in the value read at the start it sets it again; it re-enables the "SPK" pin, syncs DAPM, releases the mutex, stores the requested mode in cs35l45->amplifier_mode and returns 1. The register writes' return values are not checked.
note: Listed as cs35l45_amp_mode_put (name not in file); the real function is cs35l45_amplifier_mode_put, cs35l45.c:211-299, slice cut the head. The old prose omitted the two early return 0 conditions and the read-error return.

name: cs53l30_set_dai_tdm_slot
prose: Precondition: dai is the CS53L30 DAI; tx_mask is not used; rx_mask selects ASoC slots; slots and slot_width describe the TDM frame. Returns -EINVAL (with a logged message) if rx_mask is 0, if slots or slot_width is not positive or slot_width is above 64, if slot_width is not a multiple of 8, if rx_mask has more than CS53L30_TDM_SLOT_MAX (4) bits set, or if the last chosen slot ends beyond byte 47 (loc[last] + slot_step - 1 above 47). Otherwise it converts each set bit of rx_mask, lowest first, to a byte location loc[n] = slot_index * (slot_width / 8) and builds a 64-bit enable mask of slot_step bytes at each location (computed with int shifts 1 << slot_step and 1 << slot_next, which are undefined for shifts of 31 or more if slot_next could reach 31). It then writes loc[n] into the ASP TDM TX control register of each used channel and writes the enable mask a byte at a time into the ASP_TDMTX_EN registers, and returns 0. Register write results are not checked. The remaining unused loc entries stay at 48 and are not written.
note: slice cut the head; real function cs53l30.c:747-817. Reviewer right: 1 << slot_next (784) and 1 << slot_step (782) use int shifts; with slot_next 31 this is undefined behaviour.

name: cx20442_pm_to_v253_vls
prose: Pure helper mapping a power-management bit pattern to a V.253 voice line selection. With the AGC bit masked out of value, it returns V253_VLS_T for 0; V253_VLS_M1S1 for any of SPKOUT, MIC or SPKOUT|MIC; V253_VLS_L for TELOUT, TELIN or TELOUT|TELIN; V253_VLS_NONE for TELOUT|MIC; and -EINVAL for every other combination. The AGC bit does not affect the result.
note: cx20442.c:123-140. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits EINVAL): right; contract left empty.

name: cx20442_pm_to_v253_vsp
prose: Pure helper computing the V.253 voice speaker-phone value. If the bits other than AGC equal SPKOUT, MIC or SPKOUT|MIC, it returns 1 when the AGC bit is set and 0 when it is clear. For any other combination it returns -EINVAL if the AGC bit is set and 0 if it is clear.
note: cx20442.c:141-150. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits EINVAL): right; contract left empty.

name: es8311_hw_params
prose: Precondition: substream, params and dai belong to an ES8311 codec; es8311->mclk_freq (0 if unset) and es8311->provider (codec is clock provider) are set. Returns 0 or -EINVAL or the error of es8311_get_mclk_coeff. It maps the sample width (params_width) to a word-length code (16, 18, 20, 24, 32; any other width returns -EINVAL before any register write) and updates the word-length field of ES8311_SDP_IN for playback or ES8311_SDP_OUT for capture. It returns -EINVAL if mclk_freq exceeds ES8311_MCLK_MAX_FREQ. If mclk_freq is 0 it returns -EINVAL when the codec is the provider; otherwise it selects BCLK as the internal MCLK and uses rate * width * 2 as the mclk frequency. It looks up the coefficients with es8311_get_mclk_coeff(mclk_freq, rate, &coeff) and returns its error if no entry fits. It then updates CLKMGR1 (MCLK_SEL/MCLK_ON/BCLK_ON), returns -EINVAL (WARN_ON_ONCE) if coeff.div or coeff.div_adc_dac is 0 or above 8 or if coeff.mult is not 1, 2, 4 or 8, and updates CLKMGR2 (pre-divider and multiplier) and CLKMGR5 (ADC/DAC dividers). If provider, it computes div_lrclk = mclk_freq / rate, returns -EINVAL if that is 0 or above ES8311_CLKMGR_LRCLK_DIV_MAX + 1, writes the LRCLK divider to CLKMGR7 and CLKMGR8, returns -EINVAL if div_lrclk is not a multiple of 2 * width, and derives the BCLK divider (direct index up to ES8311_BCLK_DIV_IDX_OFFSET, otherwise looked up in es8311_bclk_divs, -EINVAL if not present) and updates CLKMGR6. Several error returns happen after earlier register updates, which are not undone. It takes no locks.
note: Listed as <unnamed hw_params handler> and dropped; the slice (es8311.c:521-777) is the tail of es8311_hw_params (481-639), a real function, so fixed. Old prose was close; rewritten from the code (note the early width check and the BCLK-as-MCLK path).

name: #define HI_U16(a)		(((a) >> 8) & 0xFF)
prose: Function-like macro, not a C function: HI_U16(a) expands to ((a) >> 8) & 0xFF, the second-lowest byte of a. The name says U16 but the result is limited to 8 bits. It evaluates a once and has no state of its own.
note: fs-amp-lib.h:11. Previously dropped; the macro does bit arithmetic, kept as a fix with the macro head as its name.

name: #define LO_U16(a)		((a) & 0xFF)
prose: Function-like macro, not a C function: LO_U16(a) expands to (a) & 0xFF, the lowest byte of a. It evaluates a once and has no state of its own.
note: fs-amp-lib.h:12. Previously dropped; the macro does bit arithmetic, kept as a fix with the macro head as its name.

name: jz4760_codec_mute_stream
prose: Precondition: dai belongs to a jz4760 codec; mute nonzero means mute the DAC. direction is unused. It picks gain_bit = REG_IFR_GDO when muting and REG_IFR_GUP when unmuting, then calls snd_soc_component_update_bits on JZ4760_CODEC_REG_CR2 to set or clear REG_CR2_DAC_MUTE. Only if that returns exactly 1 (the bit changed) it reads JZ4760_CODEC_REG_PMR2 (read result not checked); if the SB_DAC bit is set there it returns 1 immediately. Otherwise it polls JZ4760_CODEC_REG_IFR every 1000 us for up to 1 second until gain_bit is set; on timeout it logs and returns that negative error (ETIMEDOUT) without clearing the flag; on success it writes gain_bit to IFR to clear the flag. In every remaining case (no change, a negative update error, or after the flag was cleared) it reads CR2 (result unused) and returns 0. So the return value is 1 only in the SB_DAC-set case, 0 on the other normal paths, and a negative error only from the poll timeout; an update_bits error is not propagated.
note: Listed as unnamed_dac_mute; real function jz4760_codec_mute_stream, jz4760.c:249-283 (slice cut the head). Old prose correctly described the paths; rewritten from the code, nothing contradicted.

name: madera_is_syncclk
prose: Pure helper classifying a clock id. Returns 1 for MADERA_CLK_SYSCLK_1, MADERA_CLK_SYSCLK_2 and MADERA_CLK_SYSCLK_3, 0 for MADERA_CLK_ASYNCCLK_1 and MADERA_CLK_ASYNCCLK_2, and -EINVAL for every other value. No side effects.
note: madera.c:3225-3238. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits EINVAL): right; contract left empty because it depends on enum constants.

name: madera_out1_demux_put
prose: Precondition: kcontrol is the OUT1 demux enumerated control of a madera codec; ucontrol->value.enumerated.item[0] is the requested mux value. Returns -EINVAL if the item is above e->items - 1. Otherwise it takes the DAPM mutex and tests whether the EP_SEL field of MADERA_OUTPUT_ENABLES_1 would change. If it would not change it skips to the end. If it would change it disables OUT1L/OUT1R (a failure is only warned), waits 2-3 ms, and then, only if madera->out_clamp[0] is set, writes the new EP_SEL; if that write fails it logs an error and does not reprogram the mode; otherwise (including when out_clamp[0] is false, in which case no EP_SEL write is made and ret is 0) it calls madera_set_output_mode(component, 1, out_mono), with out_mono false only for a stereo headphone selection (ep_sel 0 and pdata out_mono[0] false) and true otherwise (failure only warned). Then, if ep_sel is nonzero or (out_clamp[0] is set and out_shorted[0] is clear), it restores OUT1L/OUT1R from madera->hp_ena (failure warned; waits 34 ms if hp_ena, else 2-3 ms). It releases the mutex, calls snd_soc_dapm_mux_update_power and returns its negative error if it fails; otherwise it returns the value of the changed-bits test (nonzero if the selection changed, 0 if not).
note: madera.c:541-629 (slice cut the head). Reviewer right: madera_set_output_mode is called whenever the EP_SEL write was skipped or succeeded, so also when out_clamp[0] is false (lines 579-593).

name: get_srate
prose: Pure helper mapping a sample rate to the codec's srate code: 16000 gives 3, 32000 gives 6, 48000 gives 8, any other rate returns -EINVAL. No side effects.
note: ml26124.c:293-311. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits EINVAL): right; contract left empty.

name: nau8822_calc_pll
prose: Precondition: pll_in is the PLL reference frequency, fs the sample rate, pll_param the output structure. Returns -EINVAL if pll_in is above NAU_PLL_REF_MAX or below NAU_PLL_REF_MIN. It scans nau8822_mclk_scaler[] computing f2 = 256 * fs * 4 * scaler / 10 and accepts an entry when f2 is strictly between NAU_PLL_FREQ_MIN and NAU_PLL_FREQ_MAX and larger than the current f2_max. The loop bound is the variable scal_sel, which is set to the accepted index i, so after the first accepted entry the loop condition i < scal_sel fails on the next iteration and the scan ends; in effect the first (lowest-index) valid scaler is chosen, not the one with the maximum f2 over the whole table. If no entry was accepted (scal_sel still equals the table size) it returns -EINVAL. Otherwise it stores mclk_scaler = index, computes pll_ratio = (f2 << 28) / pll_in, sets pre_factor to 0 (or to 1 and doubles the ratio when the 4-bit integer part is below NAU_PLL_OPTOP_MIN), stores pll_int = integer part (4 bits) and pll_frac = (low 28 bits) >> 4, and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function nau8822.c:616-654. Reviewer WRONG: since scal_sel is both the loop bound and the result, the loop stops at the first accepted index (627-633); the old 'smallest valid index' claim holds in effect, even though the f2_max comparison suggests a maximum search.

name: nau8825_button_decode
prose: Pure helper converting the chip's button bit field into ALSA jack button bits. For each of bits 0 to 5 of value that is set, it ORs in SND_JACK_BTN_0 to SND_JACK_BTN_5 respectively (the jack constants, e.g. SND_JACK_BTN_0 is 0x4000, not a bit position equal to the input bit); bits 6 and 7 and anything higher are ignored. Returns the combined mask, or 0 if none of bits 0..5 is set. No side effects.
note: nau8825.c:1708-1727. Reviewer right: SND_JACK_BTN_0 is 0x4000 (include/sound/jack.h:50), so a shift-by-8 contract does not describe it; contract left empty.

name: nau8825_xtalk_sidetone
prose: Precondition: sig_org and sig_cros are the original and cross-talk signal levels. Returns 0 (after a WARN_ON) if either is 0. Otherwise it takes nau8825_intlog10_dec3 of each (log10 scaled by 1000), computes gain = |log_org - log_cros| * 20 + GAIN_AUGMENT (22500) in u32, then sidetone = SIDETONE_BASE (207000) - gain * 2 in u32 arithmetic and returns sidetone / 1000. The subtraction is unsigned and is not guarded, so when gain * 2 exceeds 207000, that is when the scaled log difference exceeds 4050, the result wraps modulo 2^32 and the returned value is large.
note: nau8825.c:358-375. Reviewer WRONG: it quotes SIDETONE_BASE as 0x100000, but nau8825.c:43 defines SIDETONE_BASE 207000, so a u32 wrap is possible for large level ratios (log10 of a u32 can reach about 9.6, so differences above 4.05 are reachable). Contract left empty.

name: pcm512x_set_dividers
prose: Precondition: dai and params describe the stream; pcm512x->bclk_ratio, pll_out, pll_in and sclk are configured. It computes all clock dividers itself and writes them; it returns 0 or a negative error and may leave earlier register writes in place after an error. LRCLK divider: bclk_ratio if positive, else the frame size from params (-EINVAL if 0). If pll_out is 0 it takes sck_rate from sclk, bclk_div = sck / (rate * lrclk) rounded and mck = sck. Otherwise it needs a nonzero BCLK rate from snd_soc_params_to_bclk (its negative error or -EINVAL for 0 is returned), finds sck_rate with pcm512x_find_sck (-EINVAL if 0), finds PLL coefficients (error returned), writes PLL coefficient registers 0 to 4 (each failure returned) and uses the real PLL rate as mck. It returns -EINVAL if bclk_div is above 128 (a zero divider is not checked). It derives sample_rate = sck / bclk_div / lrclk_div, osr_rate = 16 * sample_rate and dsp_div of 2 when mck exceeds the DSP maximum, else 1. If pcm512x_pllin_dac_rate gives a nonzero dac_rate it selects the PLL input clock as the DAC source (DAC_REF and GPIO_DACIN writes, errors returned); otherwise it searches a DAC multiplier no faster than 6144000 Hz (-EINVAL if none divides) and selects SCK as the DAC source. It computes osr_div, dac_div (each -EINVAL above 128) and ncp_div (rounding, capped so the NCP clock stays at or below 2048000 Hz; -EINVAL if above 128), idac = mck / (dsp_div * sample_rate), then writes the DSP, DAC, NCP, OSR, BCLK and LRCLK divider registers (value minus 1) and the two IDAC bytes, and sets the fs speed mode (48, 96, 192 or 384 kHz class by sample_rate); any regmap failure is returned at once. Returns 0 at the end.
note: Listed as an unnamed divider-setup function (dropped); the slice (pcm512x.c:1022-1287) contains the tail of pcm512x_set_dividers (888-1164), so fixed under the real name. The old prose's precondition (dividers already computed) did not match the code, the function computes them.

name: pm4125_get_micb_vout_ctl_val
prose: Pure helper (apart from a log message): micb_mv is the requested microphone bias voltage in mV. If it is below 1600 or above 2850 it logs an error with dev_err and returns -EINVAL; otherwise it returns (micb_mv - 1600) / 50 (integer division).

name: rt5640_readable_register
prose: Regmap readable-register predicate: dev is unused and reg is a register address; returns true if the register may be read and false otherwise. It first loops over rt5640_ranges and returns true if reg lies in a range's window (window_start to window_start + window_len, inclusive) or between its range_min and range_max (inclusive). It then switches on reg and returns true for the 115 case labels it lists (RT5640 register constants, including IRQ, GPIO, DSP, and the other control registers) and false in the default case. No side effects.

name: rt5670_set_dai_pll
prose: Precondition: dai belongs to an rt5670 component, pll_id is unused, source selects the PLL input, freq_in and freq_out are in Hz. Returns 0 without any register access if (source, freq_in, freq_out) equal the cached pll_src, pll_in and pll_out. If freq_in or freq_out is 0 it logs, sets the cached pll_in and pll_out to 0 (pll_src is left as is), switches the system clock source to MCLK and returns 0, without checking source. Otherwise it selects the PLL source in RT5670_GLB_CLK: MCLK for RT5670_PLL1_S_MCLK; for RT5670_PLL1_S_BCLK1 to BCLK4 it uses BCLK1 when dai->id is RT5670_AIF1 and BCLK2 when it is RT5670_AIF2 and returns -EINVAL for any other dai->id; any other source returns -EINVAL. It then calls rl6231_pll_calc(freq_in, freq_out, &pll_code) and returns its negative error (logged) if it fails; note the source register update above has already been written in that case. On success it writes RT5670_PLL_CTRL1 and RT5670_PLL_CTRL2 from the n, k, m and bypass codes, caches freq_in, freq_out and source in pll_in, pll_out and pll_src and returns 0. The cached values are unchanged on every error return.
note: Listed name rt5670_set_pll does not exist; the real function is rt5670_set_dai_pll, rt5670.c:2528-2599 (slice cut the head). Old prose matched the code except that it did not mention the source register already being written before an rl6231_pll_calc failure.

name: rt5682s_set_component_pll
prose: Precondition: component belongs to an rt5682s codec, pll_id indexes the pll_src, pll_in and pll_out arrays (RT5682S_PLL1 or RT5682S_PLL2), source is the PLL source, freq_in and freq_out are in Hz. Returns 0 without any register access if (source, freq_in, freq_out) equal the cached values for pll_id. If freq_in or freq_out is 0 it clears the cached pll_in and pll_out for pll_id, sets the system clock source to MCLK and returns 0; this check comes before the source check, so an unknown source with a zero frequency also returns 0 (pll_src is not updated). Otherwise it selects the PLL source in RT5682S_GLB_CLK for RT5682S_PLL_S_MCLK or RT5682S_PLL_S_BCLK1 and returns -EINVAL for any other source. It then calls find_pll_inter_combination and stores the result in rt5682s->pll_comb; it returns -EINVAL unless the combination is USE_PLLA for PLL1 or USE_PLLB or USE_PLLAB for PLL2 (the source register change above is already written). It programs the PLLA registers (CTRL_1, 2, 6) for USE_PLLA or USE_PLLAB, the PLLB registers (CTRL_3, 4, 6) for USE_PLLB or USE_PLLAB and sets the PLLB source to DFIN for USE_PLLB. Finally it caches freq_in, freq_out and source for pll_id and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function rt5682s.c:2330-2425. Reviewer right: with zero freq_in or freq_out the function returns 0 (line 2341-2347) before validating source, so an invalid source returns 0, not -EINVAL.

name: rt700_headset_detect
prose: Precondition: rt700 is the codec private data with a working regmap. Returns 0, -ETIMEDOUT, -ENODEV or a negative regmap error. It reads RT700_COMBO_JACK_AUTO_CTL2 into buf with rt700_index_read; a negative result returns that error (logged). While loop < 500 and the AUTO_DET_STATUS bit of buf is clear it increments loop, sleeps 9-10 ms, re-reads the register (a negative result returns that error) and then reads the pin-sense register of RT700_HP_OUT with regmap_read, whose return value is ignored; if bit 31 of the resulting jack_status is clear it logs and returns -ENODEV. A failed pin-sense read leaves jack_status unchanged, so it is treated as removal only if the previous value (initially 0) has bit 31 clear. After the loop, if loop is 500 or more it returns -ETIMEDOUT, which also happens when the status bit became set during the 500th poll. Otherwise it sets rt700->jack_type to SND_JACK_HEADPHONE if the TRS bit is set, else to SND_JACK_HEADSET if the CTIA or OMTP bit is set (jack_type is left unchanged if none is set) and returns 0.
note: rt700.c:106-154. Reviewer right on both points: loop >= 500 (133) takes the timeout path even if the bit was just set, and the regmap_read result at 128 is ignored, so -ENODEV depends on a stale or zero jack_status.

name: ssm3515_set_tdm_slot
prose: Precondition: dai belongs to an ssm3515 component; only tx_mask (one slot) is supported. Returns -EINVAL if tx_mask is 0, rx_mask is nonzero, tx_mask has more than one bit set, or slot_width is not 16, 24, 32, 48 or 64 (mapped to bclks codes 0 to 4). Otherwise it updates the TDM_BCLKS field of SSM3515_SAI1 and returns its negative error if that fails; then it updates the TDM_SLOT field of SSM3515_SAI2 with the lowest set bit index of tx_mask and returns its negative error if that fails; else it returns 0. The slots argument is not used. If the SAI2 update fails, the SAI1 field has already been changed and the SAI2 field is not guaranteed unchanged.
note: slice cut the head; real function ssm3515.c:296-345. Reviewer right: nothing in the code restores SAI1 or guarantees SAI2 is untouched after an SAI2 update failure.

name: sti_sas_init_sas_registers
prose: Precondition: component and data are the sti-sas codec and its data. Returns the final ret of snd_soc_component_update_bits calls: negative error, or 0, or 1 when the last executed update changed a register. It first clears the SPDIF bi-phase enable bits in STIH407_AUDIO_GLUE_CTRL; only if that call returned 0 (no change) does it also clear the bi-phase idle value bits. A negative result from either logs and returns it. Then it sets STIH407_DAC_STANDBY_MASK in STIH407_AUDIO_DAC_CTRL; the second update (STIH407_DAC_STANDBY_ANA_MASK) is executed only if the previous update returned 0, and the third (STIH407_DAC_SOFTMUTE_MASK) only if the second was executed and returned 0, because each is guarded by if (!ret) and update_bits returns 1 when a bit changed. A negative result logs and returns it; otherwise it returns ret, so the return value can be 1 and later updates may have been skipped.
note: sti-sas.c:99-142. Reviewer WRONG: the third DAC update is guarded by if (!ret) at line 131, not unconditional; the guard skips it whenever the previous update reported a change (ret 1).

name: tasdevice_select_tuningprm_cfg
prose: Precondition: context is a tasdevice_priv; prm_no is the program index, cfg_no the configuration index, rca_conf_no the RCA configuration index; when the checks below pass, rca->cfg_info[rca_conf_no] must be non-NULL because it is dereferenced (only the cfg_info array pointer is tested). Returns an int that is prog_status, the number of devices for which a program load was requested in the first loop; it is 0 on every early exit and never a negative error code. It logs and returns 0 if tas_priv->fmw is NULL, if cfg_no is not below nr_configurations, if prm_no is not below nr_programs (negative values of cfg_no and prm_no are not rejected here), or if rca_conf_no is negative, not below rca->ncfgs, or cfg_info is NULL. Otherwise for each device i below ndev: if its bit is set in cfg_info[rca_conf_no]->active_dev and prm_no >= 0 and (its cur_prog differs from prm_no or force_fwload_status is set) it sets cur_conf to -1, is_loading to true and counts prog_status; devices not in active_dev get is_loading false; is_loaderr is cleared for all. If prog_status is nonzero it loads programs[prm_no] with tasdevice_load_data and sets cur_prog = prm_no for devices that are loading and had no load error. It then marks as loading each device with cfg_no >= 0, cur_conf different from cfg_no, active and without load error; if any, it loads configs[cfg_no], and for each loaded device without error calls tasdev_load_calibrated_data and sets cur_conf = cfg_no (error bits are accumulated into the local status, which is not returned and not used afterwards). Returns prog_status.

name: tfa989x_find_sample_rate
prose: Precondition: rate is a sample rate in Hz. Scans tfa989x_rates in order and returns the index of the first entry equal to rate, or -EINVAL if none matches. No side effects.

name: twl4030_hw_params
prose: Precondition: substream, params and dai belong to a twl4030 codec. Returns 0 or -EINVAL. If params_channels is 4 it reads the audio interface and codec mode registers and, only if the mode has TWL4030_OPTION_1 set and the interface format is TDM, calls twl4030_tdm_enable(component, stream, 1); otherwise it returns -EINVAL. If twl4030->configured is already set it returns 0 without further work. Otherwise it reads the codec mode (with CODECPDZ masked), maps the rate to an APLL rate code (8000, 11025, 12000, 16000, 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100, 48000, 96000; any other rate logs and returns -EINVAL) and the sample width to a data-width code (16 and 32 only, other widths log and return -EINVAL). If either register value differs from the current one it writes the codec mode and audio interface registers (toggling the codec off and on with twl4030_codec_enable around the writes when codec_powered is set). It then sets configured = 1 and stores rate, sample_bits (minimum of the SAMPLE_BITS interval) and channels, and, if twl4030->slave_substream is set, calls twl4030_constraints(twl4030, substream) to constrain the other stream; it returns 0. The twl4030_tdm_enable call for four channels may already have changed hardware state when a later check returns -EINVAL.
note: twl4030.c:1691-1807 (slice cut the head). Reviewer WRONG: the code does call twl4030_constraints at line 1804 when slave_substream is set.

name: uda1334_set_fmt

It masks fmt to the format, inversion and clock-provider fields and returns -EINVAL (with an error log) unless the result is exactly SND_SOC_DAIFMT_I2S | SND_SOC_DAIFMT_NB_NF | SND_SOC_DAIFMT_CBC_CFC; otherwise it returns 0. It does not write any hardware or state.

name: wcd_correct_swch_plug
prose: Work handler: work is the correct_plug_swch member of a wcd_mbhc. Returns nothing. It calls pm_runtime_get_sync on the codec; if that returns a negative value other than -EACCES it logs, calls pm_runtime_put_noidle and returns without doing anything else. Otherwise it reads the micbias voltage and the headset threshold and masks the headset-insert ADC interrupt (disable_irq_nosync). It checks cross connection swap_thr times with wcd_check_cross_conn (the last result counts); if it is positive the plug type becomes MBHC_PLUG_TYPE_GND_MIC_SWAP and it skips the first measurement. Otherwise it measures the ADC continuously, derives the plug type, and immediately reports a headphone, or reports a headset and sets ADC mode and ADC enable fields to 0 and DETECTION_DONE to 1. At correct_plug_type it disables BCS slow-insertion detection and loops for HS_DETECT_PLUG_TIME_MS: if hs_detect_work_stop is set it disables the micbias and jumps to exit (skipping the final report); each pass sleeps 180 ms, measures ADC once, re-derives the plug type, handles a special headset (threshold rescaled by the micbias ratio) and, when the reading is at or below the threshold with the headphone amp off, re-checks cross connection (counting swap detections up to swap_thr, resetting the count and re-deriving the type when there is none, continuing on errors or when the swap callback reports failure); a reading above the threshold, or force_linein, sets MBHC_PLUG_TYPE_HIGH_HPH. After the loop it re-enables BCS, turns a HIGH_HPH into HEADSET for a special headset or enables the electrical current source otherwise, clears ADC mode and enable, reports the plug type, sets DETECTION_DONE for a headset (clears it otherwise) and updates the FSM source when a micbias control callback exists. At exit it disables micbias 2 through the callback if present; if the plug type is MBHC_PLUG_TYPE_HEADPHONE it disables the micbias and re-enables the headset-insert interrupt (this is the only place in the function where that interrupt is re-enabled); it calls hph_pull_down_ctrl(true) if the callback exists and finally pm_runtime_put_autosuspend.

name: wcd9335_codec_enable_dec
prose: DAPM event handler for a decimator widget: w is the widget (its name is expected to look like "<prefix> <name containing the decimator number>"), kc the kcontrol, event a DAPM event. Returns -ENOMEM if the first 15 characters of w->name cannot be duplicated; -EINVAL if the name does not yield a decimator index (the name is split at the first space and the text after it is searched with strpbrk for a digit 0 to 8, then converted with kstrtouint; failures log and return -EINVAL; the pointer after the space is not checked for NULL before strpbrk); otherwise 0 for every event, handled or not (ret holds the 0 from kstrtouint). Registers used are the TX path control, HPF gate, config 0 and volume control for decimator n at a stride of 16. On SND_SOC_DAPM_PRE_PMU it looks up the analog mic input of the decimator, and if there is one with a power-level register, sets the decimator power level (low power, high performance or default) from that level; it forces the HPF cut-off to CF_MIN_3DB_150HZ when it is different, sets the TX PGA mute bit (0x10) and the APC bit (0x08). On POST_PMU it opens the HPF gate, for decimator 0 writes the MBHC ZDET ramp control sequence 0x83, 0xA3, 0x83, 0x03, then restores the HPF gate, clears the mute bit and rewrites the gain register with its own value. On PRE_PMD it saves the HPF cut-off, sets mute, clears APC and, if the cut-off was not 150 Hz, rewrites the saved cut-off. On POST_PMD it clears the mute bit. The register accesses' results are not checked.

name: wcd934x_wcd_mbhc_calc_impedance
prose: Precondition: component is a wcd934x codec with MBHC set up; zl and zr point to u32 outputs for the left and right impedance in ohms. Returns nothing. It saves the BTN5, BTN6, BTN7, MBHC_CTL_CLK and NEW_ZDET_ANA_CTL registers; if the ELECT FSM bit (0x80) is set it clears it and remembers that; for a NO-jack hphl_swh configuration it clears L_DET_EN; it turns off the 100k pull-down on HPHL. It measures the left channel with a first ramp (parameter set 1) and, if a second ramp is required, repeats with the parameter set chosen from the first result (below 32 ohm set 0, 400 to 1200 ohm set 2, above 1200 ohm set 3). *zl becomes WCD934X_ZDET_FLOATING_IMPEDANCE if the result is the floating value or above 100k, else the result in ohms (z1L / 1000) adjusted by wcd934x_wcd_mbhc_qfuse_cal. It then does the same for the right channel (the second ramp is skipped in some cases), setting *zr similarly. If both are floating it stops measuring (invalid plug or extension cable). If either is floating or one side is below and the other above WCD_MONO_HS_MIN_THR it sets the hph type to mono and stops. Otherwise it grounds the right PA, measures the left channel again (z1Ls, with parameter set 0 or 1 chosen by *zl), releases the grounding, and compares it with the parallel of *zl and 9 ohm to set the hph type to stereo or mono. On every path it ends at zdet_complete, where it restores BTN5, BTN6 and BTN7, turns the HPHL 100k pull-down back on, re-enables L_DET_EN for NO-jack, restores NEW_ZDET_ANA_CTL and MBHC_CTL_CLK from the saved values and, if it had cleared it, sets the ELECT FSM bit again.
note: slice cut the head; real function wcd934x.c:2699-2868. Reviewer WRONG: MBHC_CTL_CLK, NEW_ZDET_ANA_CTL and the ELECT FSM bit are restored at 2864-2867 on every path (all branches reach zdet_complete). The zdet_ramp and qfuse_cal helpers were not read.

name: fll_factors
prose: Precondition: fll_div is the output structure, input and output are frequencies in Hz. Returns -EINVAL (after a printk) if output is not in one of the ranges 2815250-3125000, 5625000-6250000, 11250000-12500000 or 22500000-25000000 Hz, which select fll_div->div 4, 3, 2 and 1 respectively. Otherwise it sets ratio to 1 if input is above 48000 and 8 if not, computes t1 = output * (1 << (div + 1)) and t2 = input * ratio, sets n = t1 / t2 and, if the remainder Nmod is nonzero, computes K as the low 32 bits of FIXED_FLL_SIZE * Nmod / t2 (64-bit division), adds 5 to K only when K % 10 is at least 5, divides K by 10 and stores it in k; with a zero remainder k is 0. It returns 0. The rounding step is conditional, not an unconditional +5. t2 is not checked for zero.
note: wm8350.c:973-1019. Reviewer right: the +5 happens only when K % 10 >= 5 (line 1009).

name: wm8524_set_fmt

name: wm8753_set_dai
prose: Precondition: kcontrol is the DAI-mode enum control of a wm8753 component; ucontrol->value.enumerated.item[0] is the requested dai_func. Returns 0 without changes if the requested value equals wm8753->dai_func. Returns -EBUSY if the component is active (snd_soc_component_active). Otherwise it reads WM8753_IOCTL, stores the requested value in wm8753->dai_func, and if bits 2..3 of the register already equal the new value it returns 1 without writing anything. If they differ it writes the register with the mode field (bits 2..3) replaced (other bits kept per the mask 0x1f3), rewrites the HiFi and voice DAI formats with wm8753_hifi_write_dai_fmt and wm8753_voice_write_dai_fmt using the saved formats and returns 1. The write results are not checked.
